rationale: ExprTyped gives exactly the Give, Construct and Weaken alternatives. Give uses static take; Construct selects the declared field classes and ArgsTyped threads environments left to right, requiring a whole type for each argument and matching the argument count; Weaken retains the post-environment and applies Subtype to the result. The empty ArgsTyped rule leaves the environment unchanged. Explicit Admissible and environment-well-formedness premises implement the chapter's prior well-formed/normalized-type convention; none requires Eval, successful execution, or a heap witness. Constructor arguments are whole declared types even if an untyped construction could store a partial object. unit:given.typing.environments introduces Gamma and take, unit:given.typing.forgetting introduces the weakening relation, unit:given.typing.declarations introduces Sigma and class erasure, and unit:given.evaluation fixes the corresponding runtime argument order.
